Let's introduce the new variable $u=2x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(7)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\ln(7)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(7)}}\frac{1}{8}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \frac{1}{8}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(7)}}e^{2x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \frac{1}{8}\int_{0}^{2\ln(7)}e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{32}\int_{0}^{2\ln(7)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{32}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{2\ln(7)} \\ & = \frac{1}{32}(e^{2\ln(7)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{1}{32}(49-1) \\ & = \frac{48}{32} \\ & = \frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=4x+3.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{d}u=4\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $3$ | $7$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{1}4\cdot 4^{4x+3}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int_{3}^{7}4^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{4^{u}}{\ln(4)}\big|_{3}^{7} \\ & = \frac{1}{\ln(4)}(4^{7}-4^{3}) \\ & = \frac{1}{\ln(4)}(16384-64) \\ & = \frac{16320}{\ln{\left(4 \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=4e^{x}+3.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4e^{x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{d}u=4e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $\ln(4)$ | $\ln(7)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $19$ | $31$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\ln(4)}^{\ln(7)}\frac{12e^{x}}{4e^{x}+3}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int_{\ln(4)}^{\ln(7)}\frac{3}{4e^{x}+3}\cdot 4e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \int_{19}^{31}\frac{3}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 3\int_{19}^{31}\frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 3\ln|u|\big|_{19}^{31} \\ & = 3(\ln(31)-\ln(19)) \\ & = 3 \ln{\left(\frac{31}{19} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$
